body:
QUESTION FOR THE LEAD AND THE ADVISOR, P2-29 (2 of 2): "STRINGS IN ENGLISH AND ARABIC" HAS NO PLACE TO LIVE YET, plus facts for the build. Nothing is built. READ, not run.

THE ARABIC CONFLICT
* The app has no localisation at all: no flutter_localizations, no supportedLocales or Localizations, no Arabic text anywhere in app/lib (checked). Localisation is listed as LATER (docs/03 line 82 "French and Arabic first", docs/08 line 344); docs/04 line 170 only promises "UI strings in one file from day one so translations are a later drop-in" (not true of the code today).
* The card's line is S-16's line, and `describeDownload` (domain/download_line.dart) is English only and is THE one phrasing. The drawing's Arabic lines ("12 من 217 على هذا الهاتف · 40 جاهزة على خادمك") therefore need that function and its words localised, which changes the in-app line of every screen (Library, playlist and album headers, Settings > Downloads) and must also work in the background isolate (no BuildContext, no Localizations). The alternative is a second phrasing for the card, which the brief forbids. Either is an ADR-level choice (docs/30 question 8), beyond size M.
* The drawing gives Arabic only for the card's own sentences; the S-16 sentences it did not draw (waiting for Wi-Fi / for your server, paused: storage limit, phone almost full, "Waiting its turn on your server", "Getting ready to download", "Downloaded - N songs", "N songs did not come" in the line itself) would be my own Arabic, unreviewed.
OPTIONS
1. English now. The Arabic stays in the drawing as the design of the later localisation; the card's words sit in ONE table (a words class, English), so a later Arabic table is a drop-in; tests pin the English. Recommended, with a new item "Localisation, Arabic first" whose fixtures are the drawing's data-ar strings.
2. A minimal words layer with an English and an Arabic table for the card AND the S-16 line, chosen from the phone's language (touches every screen's line; undrawn Arabic needs a native check).
3. The localisation plumbing first, as its own item, then P2-29 uses it.
Question: 1, 2 or 3?

FACTS FOR THE BUILD (whatever the answers)
* The bar in the drawing is (songs on the phone + songs ready on the server) / (2 x songs): 12 on the phone + 40 ready of 217 gives 52/434 = 12 %, the drawn bar. It needs a floor that only moves forward while the same jobs run.
* `import.progress` is published FLAT by the server (imports/service.py around line 405: `importId, state, total, matched, unmatched, pending, kept`), while docs/17 section 4 says `{im, counts}`; the app does not consume it (no `import.progress` anywhere in app/lib). The card would poll `GET imports` (the page polls every 3 s only while it is open: `encoreImportsProvider` is autoDispose) through one always-on watcher that polls only while an import runs and is nudged by a start, a resume and (later) that event.
* Two import paths exist: the Encore server's (`EncoreImport`, ServerKind.encore, the product) and the legacy fetch service (`ImportsController`, its end is news, `alertsImports`). I will cover the Encore server's and leave the legacy one untouched unless told otherwise.
* An import's server stage is `kept` of `matched` (Finding songs: matched + unmatched of total, while `pending` > 0); an import is `done` when nothing waits to be matched while keeping goes on, so its card ends when kept reaches matched.
* Ready to build as soon as the two answers are in: domain card model and words + tests first, the Downloads channel and the card in LocalNotifications (a method-channel recorder test), the always-on watcher, the permission asked at the first Import, the lifecycle rule, the docs rows, the amended PB-38 and ADR-R44.
